gap: No result ChatGPT got states a named heat or power measurement for any front-and-rear camera under $150: a DashCamTalk member measured 82.4 °C at the 70mai A810S's microSD slot after about 30 minutes parked facing the sun with no shutdown, and another measured the Vantrue S1 Pro drawing about 0.8 to 1.0 A at 5.1 V with both cameras recording.
standout_why: I opened dashpicked.com (cited), dashcamtalk.com/best-dash-cams (cited), knowledgelib.io (cited), carcody.com (cited), productbible.com and both Smart Home Hookup roundups. None gives a temperature, power-draw or bitrate measurement for an under-$150 two-channel camera; dashpicked and productbible carry only maker specs and Amazon review tallies, and DashCamTalk's roundup carries only editorial scores. The one overlap is knowledgelib (cited), which already relays GameRevolution's finding that the A810 Lite's front camera drops from 30 fps to 24/25 fps when both cameras record, so that part rates 1. Three pages could not be opened and are unchecked: Car and Driver's under-$170 page (cited), vortexradar.com (HTTP 403) and thecargearguide.com (certificate error). The measurements are single-unit readings by different forum members, not one lab's side-by-side test.
decides: It confirms rather than changes the pick. The A810S heat reading supports ChatGPT's first answer on the hot-weather point (supercapacitor, no shutdown at 82.4 °C at the card slot). DashCamTalk's listing of the original A810 with a 500 mAh battery cuts against ChatGPT's second answer, which put the A810 first while saying a supercapacitor is preferable. The A810 Lite's measured 24 fps front in 2-channel mode qualifies its '4K front' claim. For the row we can link, the Vantrue S1 Pro 2CH ($135.99 in the brief's 2026-11-21 partner table, not re-read by me), the only named numbers are a 2023 forum power reading and The Hook Up's day and night plate comparison against the Viofo A119 Mini 2. No measurement shows it beating the A810S, so it wins at most a segment (2.5K front with a partner link), not the question on measured grounds.

findings.label: Surface temperatures after about 30 minutes parked facing the sun (measured by DashCamTalk member Augustus, post dated 2026-04-03)
findings.value: 82.4 °C at the microSD slot; 70.1 °C on the LCD; 64.5 °C on the top grille; 60.1 °C on the underside grille; camera did not shut down
findings.source_title: 70mai A810S 4K Review LN (DashCamTalk forum, post #6 heat test)
findings.note: Conditions: mid-afternoon, cabin 32.7 °C, weather-bureau outside temperature 28.1 °C, dashboard 53.5 °C, camera powered through the UP04 4G hardwire kit. One unit, one session; the post does not name the thermometer.

findings.label: Front-camera bitrate, file size and Wi-Fi transfer speed (measured by DashCamTalk member LateralNW, post dated 2026-01-13)
findings.value: about 29.4 Mb/s at 3840 × 2160, 30 fps, HEVC; about 210 MB per one-minute clip; about 20 MB/s over Wi-Fi
findings.note: Front channel only; the post gives no rear bitrate and no 1-channel against 2-channel frame-rate comparison. 29.4 Mb/s × 60 s ÷ 8 = 220 MB per minute, consistent with the 210 MB quoted. The same post says the A810S uses a supercapacitor and that parking modes work only with a hardwire kit installed.

findings.label: Recorded files with front and rear running together (measured by DashCamTalk member rcg530, post dated 2026-05-08)
findings.note: rcg530: 'The front camera frame rate is dropped from 30 fps in 1-channel mode to 24 fps in 2-channel mode.' The thread's power-draw and parking-time tables are images I could not read, so no wattage is given here.

findings.label: Front frame rate in dual-channel mode, as a cited rival page already reports it
findings.value: 30 fps drops to 24/25 fps when both cameras record (attributed to GameRevolution)
findings.source_title: Best Front and Rear Dash Cams Under $200 (2026) | knowledgelib.io
findings.note: This is the one named measurement on a page ChatGPT cited that overlaps this angle. I did not open GameRevolution's review itself.

findings.label: Current draw at the USB input (measured by DashCamTalk member DT MI, post dated 2023-09-04)
findings.value: about 0.8 to 1.0 A at 5.1 V with front and rear recording, Wi-Fi and screen off; peak 1.5 A at 5.1 V with Wi-Fi and screen on; 0.31 A at 5.1 V front only with no card
findings.source_title: Yet Another Vantrue S1-Pro Unboxing, Review, and Impression - Part 2 (DashCamTalk forum)
findings.note: Arithmetic: 0.8 to 1.0 A × 5.1 V = 4.1 to 5.1 W; 1.5 A × 5.1 V = 7.65 W; 0.31 A × 5.1 V = 1.6 W. The author marks the 0.8 to 1.0 A figure 'Average(?)'. No parking-mode current is given. The same post gives no temperature figure, only 'Camera runs kind of hot'. A 2023 unit; firmware has changed since.

findings.label: Parking-mode behaviour observed by DT MI (2023-09-04)
findings.value: entered parking mode after 5 minutes without movement; a motion event saved 15 seconds before the trigger plus 30 seconds after (45-second clips)
findings.source_title: Yet Another Vantrue S1-Pro Unboxing, Review, and Impression - Part 2 (DashCamTalk forum)
findings.note: Observation, not a maker spec. The post does not say which hardwire kit was used.

findings.label: Plate capture against the Viofo A119 Mini 2, which uses the same Sony IMX675 sensor (The Hook Up, 2024-12-19)
findings.value: By day the two were 'almost identical' and neither produced a fully legible plate on a passing car; at night the Viofo's HDR was better tuned for plates
findings.source_title: Ultimate Dash Cam Comparison 2024 (The Smart Home Hookup / The Hook Up)
findings.note: Qualitative ranking, no count or distance. The S1 Pro cost $159.99 in that test and did not advance from the budget round; the 1-channel Viofo A119 Mini 2 won it. The article's '0.64 watts in 2 channel' parking figure belongs to 'the Vantrue' among its top four cameras (the N4 Pro), not the S1 Pro, so it must not be used for the S1 Pro.

findings.label: DashCamTalk's database listing for the original A810 (community snapshot dated 2026-05-23)
findings.value: Front 31.0 Mbps, rear 8.0 Mbps, both at 25 fps; 500 mAh battery, with 'Battery instead of capacitor' listed as a weakness; parking mode non-buffered; operating range -10 °C to 60 °C; front Sony STARVIS 2 IMX678, rear SmartSens SC200AI
findings.note: The page does not say whether the bitrates were measured or taken from the maker, so treat them as DashCamTalk's listed figures. Its scores: day video 9/10, night video 7/10, reliability 6/10.

findings.label: What the opened rival pages measure
findings.value: dashpicked.com, productbible.com and dashcamtalk.com/best-dash-cams give no measured figure for any camera; carcody.com gives one measured field of view, for the 70mai T800 (146° front), with no tester named
findings.source_title: 4K Front and Rear Dash Cams Under $150: Five Picks Compared
findings.note: Also read on 2026-11-21: https://dashcamtalk.com/best-dash-cams/, https://productbible.com/blog/best-front-and-rear-dash-cams, https://carcody.com/best-dash-cams-of-2026-top-front-and-rear-car-cameras-for-every-budget/. dashpicked's figures are listing specs and Amazon review tallies.

A search summary mentioned blue fringing on plate characters; I did not open it and it is left out.
vortexradar.com/best-dashcams (HTTP 403), thecargearguide.com, dashanddrive.com (both certificate errors) and garagerated.com (not attempted) were not read, so they are unchecked for measurements.

Any named measurement (bitrate, power draw, temperature, plate legibility) for the DDPAI Z50 Pro Dual, DDPAI N3 Pro, Botslab G980H 4K + 2K Dual, ROVE R2-4K Dual, 70mai A510, REDTIGER or Pelsee P1 Pro: one search each surfaced only maker claims, buyer-review summaries or a DashCamTalk thread on the older DDPAI Z50; none was opened.
Parking-mode power draw for the Vantrue S1 Pro and the 70mai A810S: DT MI gives no parking current, and rcg530's A810 Lite power tables are images.
Rear-camera bitrate and 2-channel front frame rate for the 70mai A810S: LateralNW's post gives the front channel only; a search summary quoted 10.1 Mb/s rear but I did not open that post.
Today's prices for the 70mai A810S, A810, A810 Lite and ROVE R2-4K Dual: not read in this angle. I ran no store or Amazon check; the Vantrue S1 Pro 2CH $135.99 is from the brief's partner table.
